rules.title: Berkeley ban on the sale and use of coordinated pricing algorithms (Ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords, or to use, a coordinated pricing algorithm. That is any computational process that uses non-public Competitor Data to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms for future leases in coordination between a landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor. Excluded: aggregated, anonymous reports that make no recommendations; tools that set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; and market research for project financing, appraisal, or research, testing and training for software development, provided the data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated. The chapter does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge and does not bar software that helps landlords manage units generally or through public data.
rules.key_value: Competitor Data = non-public rent, occupancy and lease-date data on other properties that is less than 90 days old

coverage.summary: Applies to sellers and users of coordinated pricing algorithms for residential dwelling units in Berkeley; no unit-count or building-age limits stated in the passages.

rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated anonymous reporting products, affordable-housing rent/income limit tools, and market research, appraisal, or software research, testing and training uses (as defined in § 13.63.020).
rules.effective_date_note: The passages do not include the ordinance's own effective-date clause. A secondary source (DX06) says the chapter is 'effective January 2026'; the ordinance is Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S.
rules.quoted_span: ordinance prohibits the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms for the purpose of setting rents on residential dwelling units in the city of Berkeley
rules.review_note: The text of § 13.63.030 is truncated in the passages, so the exact prohibition wording, penalties and enforcement are not shown. The effective date comes only from a secondary source and should be checked against the ordinance text.
rules.source_notes: The secondary law-firm summary (DX06) says the chapter prohibits coordinated pricing algorithms, with recurring unit/month violations and private remedies. It also says RealPage, Inc. v. City of Berkeley was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice in January 2026.
